title: City of Toledo Bay View Water Reclamation Facility
warnings: THE PDF IS TWO SEPARATELY-PAGINATED DOCUMENTS BOUND INTO ONE FILE, AND THAT FULLY EXPLAINS THE "91 pages vs. Total Pages: 51" DISCREPANCY. Sheet 1's footer prints "Total Pages: 51" and that is exactly correct for the ISSUED PERMIT alone: PDF pages 0-50 (0-indexed) print their own "Page 2" through "Page 51" footers (sheet 1 itself is unnumbered), 51 pages total, ending mid Part III General Conditions. PDF page 51 (0-indexed) then restarts at "Page 1 of 40" under a new header, "Fact Sheet for NPDES Permit Renewal, Toledo Bay View Water Reclamation, 2023" — a 40-page Fact Sheet (40 CFR 124.8/124.56 document) bound in as PDF pages 51-90, ending at its own "Page 40 of 40". 51 + 40 = 91, the PDF's actual page count. The Fact Sheet carries Public Notice No. 191407, dated 2023-11-02, comment period ending 2023-12-02 — it is the rationale document for THIS permit action, not a stray attachment. Ohio EPA's DAM host evidently concatenates the issued instrument and its Fact Sheet into one PDF at this URL; nothing was mis-captured. The permit block below transcribes the issued instrument (sheets 1-51, Parts I-III); facts pulled from the bound Fact Sheet are held in bound_fact_sheet below and cited to their own "Page N of 40", never conflated with a permit sheet number.

THE PERMIT'S OWN CSO-STATION COUNT DISAGREES WITH ITSELF: "26" in the boilerplate intro, but only 25 stations are actually enumerated. Part I,B.2 (sheet 7) opens: "The monitoring tables for the 26 CSO sampling stations listed in Part II, Item B. of this permit are identical to this one..." Part II, Item F (sheets 23-24) then enumerates CSO sampling stations by name, location and receiving water, and that list has exactly 25 entries (2PF00000004 through 2PF00000069 — see cso_stations below). The bound Fact Sheet resolves the gap rather than deepening it: its own Facility Description (Page 7 of 40) states in plain prose "as well as 25 combined sewer overflows (CSOs), in the collection system" — agreeing with Item F, not with the "26" in Part I,B.2 — and its Table 6 (CSO Occurrence, Page 23 of 40) lists a station "026" explicitly marked "(eliminated)" with a discharge history that runs to zero and stays there. 25 active + 1 eliminated = 26, so "26" is very likely a stale figure the boilerplate never updated after 026 was retired, and Item F's list is the current, controlling one. Separately, Table 6's own footnote reads "*No discharges from CSO 011 have been reported in last five years" — 011 IS still in Item F's active list (East Side PS) and in Part II Item B, it is simply quiet; it is not the source of the miscount. Transcribed as printed; the discrepancy is the document's, not this extraction's.

FOUR DIFFERENT MERCURY NUMBERS APPEAR IN THIS PERMIT AND ARE EASY TO CONFLATE — do not average or substitute between them. (1) 1700 ng/l — the Part I,A.1 table's DAILY MAXIMUM at outfall 001 (sheet 3), whose paired 0.84 kg/day loading checks out against 130 MGD design flow. (2) 3.9 ng/l — the SAME table's MONTHLY AVERAGE limit (sheet 3; load 0.0019 kg/day, also checks out); Item X (sheet 31) itself never prints this number, only cross-referencing "the effluent limitations for mercury... given in Part I, A." — it is the bound Fact Sheet (Page 15 of 40) and its own Table 17 (Basis column "VAR (avg.)," Page 37 of 40) that identify 3.9 ng/l by name as the current VARIANCE-BASED limit, determined from the dataset's PEQmax (see bound_fact_sheet.mercury_variance_calculation and .table_17_final_effluent_limits below for exactly which date range attaches to which calculation). (3) 12 ng/l — the ANNUAL AVERAGE ceiling the permittee must hold to keep the variance in force (Item X.1.f and X.2.a; a value the permittee's own data shows it already beats — see Item X's opening paragraph, "currently able to achieve an annual average mercury concentration of 12 ng/l"). (4) 1.3 ng/l — the UNDERLYING WQBEL that is NOT in the permit's Part I,A table at all; per Item X.2.c it only attaches if the permittee lets the 12 ng/l condition lapse without seeking a new variance or modification within 6 months. All four are printed verbatim below at their sheet citations.

THE AUTHORIZATION SENTENCE (sheet 1) NAMES THREE RECEIVING WATERS AND GIVES NO RIVER MILE FOR ANY OF THEM — the mirror image of the mansfield precedent's defect (blank name, present river mile). It reads "...to the Maumee River, the Ottawa River and Swan Creek in accordance with the conditions specified in Parts I, II, and III of this permit," with no "(River Mile N.NN)" anywhere in the sentence or elsewhere in the issued permit (checked: "River Mile" occurs exactly once in the whole 91-page PDF). The only river mile in this corpus — 1.0, for the Maumee — comes from the bound Fact Sheet's "LOCATION OF DISCHARGE" section (Page 6 of 40) and is NOT a statement of the issued permit; see bound_fact_sheet.river_mile below. No river mile is given anywhere for the Ottawa River or Swan Creek outfalls (i.e., the CSOs discharging to them).

THE PART II ITEM B SAMPLING-STATION TABLE (sheet 22) GIVES DMS COORDINATES FOR ONLY 2 OF ITS 12 LISTED STATION GROUPS. 2PF00000001 and 2PF00000002 carry coordinates; 004-069, 300, 581, 586, 588, 601, 602, 603, 801 and 901 carry only a text description, no lat/long. (Contrast Part II Item F, sheets 23-24, which DOES carry a DMS pair for every one of the 25 individual CSO stations — see cso_stations below.) Recorded as an absence, not filled in from any outside source.

MINOR DOCUMENT-LEVEL DEFECTS, transcribed as printed rather than silently corrected. (a) Item F's DMS table (sheet 24) prints station 2PF00000048 (Hillside and Chester St) at "41 N 38' 97", 83 W 34' 37"" — 97 seconds is not a valid DMS value (max 59.999...); the document's own arithmetic error, not a transcription artifact. (b) Part II Item R (sheet 29) prints "sampling at station 2PF000000001" — nine zeros between "2PF" and the final "1" where the station ID format takes eight (2PF00000001); an extra digit, document's own typo. (c) The Item F public-access-area table (sheet 24) lists "Cullen Park" as an Area Name with no Description of Location and no Associated CSO — the row is simply incomplete on the page. (d) The Director's signature block (sheet 1) prints her name as "Anne M. V ogel" with an interior space inside "Vogel" — almost certainly a font-kerning artifact of this text layer rather than a second name, but transcribed exactly as it renders; her name is given below as printed on the signature line.

fields.facility_name: City of Toledo Bay View Water Reclamation Facility
fields.facility_name_note: Printed both as "City of Toledo Bay View Water Reclamation wastewater treatment works" (sheet 1, authorization sentence) and "Toledo Bay View Water Reclamation Facility (Toledo WRF)" (bound Fact Sheet, Page 1 and Page 6 of 40); the fact sheet's applicant line separately names "City of Toledo Public Utilities" as the applying department. One facility, three labels for it in this file; not a discrepancy worth a warning.
fields.permit_action_source: Not stated in the word "renewal" on the authorization page itself (sheet 1 uses only "is authorized... to discharge"). The label comes from the bound Fact Sheet's own title, "Fact Sheet for NPDES Permit Renewal, Toledo Bay View Water Reclamation, 2023," and its "SUMMARY OF PERMIT CONDITIONS" section (Page 2 of 40), which describes changes relative to "the current permit." [inference] from the bound Fact Sheet, not a literal quote of the issued instrument.
fields.facility_address: 3900 N. Summit St., Toledo, Ohio, Lucas County
fields.receiving_water_quote: "...is authorized by the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency, hereinafter referred to as 'Ohio EPA,' to discharge from the City of Toledo Bay View Water Reclamation wastewater treatment works located at 3900 N. Summit St., Toledo, Ohio, Lucas County (and associated combined sewer overflows) to the Maumee River, the Ottawa River and Swan Creek in accordance with the conditions specified in Parts I, II, and III of this permit." (Permit 2PF00000*OD, sheet 1) See warnings[3]: no river mile is given for any of the three.
fields.receiving_water_by_discharge_point: The three named waters resolve to specific discharge points only through Part II Item B (outfall 001 and plant bypass 002, both "...discharge to Maumee River") and Item F (each of the 25 individual CSO stations, tagged with its own receiving water — see cso_stations below). Tally from Item F: 15 CSOs to Maumee River, 7 to Swan Creek, 3 to Ottawa River (15+7+3 = 25, agreeing with the station count in warnings[1]). So the plant's own final effluent and its headworks bypass discharge ONLY to the Maumee; the Ottawa River and Swan Creek in the authorization sentence are entirely a function of where the combined-sewer system's overflow points happen to sit.
fields.total_pages_note: The issued permit's own printed count (sheet 1 footer, "Total Pages: 51"), and correct for the issued instrument alone. See warnings[0] for the full 91-page PDF / bound Fact Sheet resolution.
fields.renewal_application_due: The permit's own text requires submission "no later than 180 days prior to the above date of expiration" — i.e. on or about 2028-08-04 for the 2029-01-31 expiration. [inference] from the permit's stated rule (sheet 1); the permit prints no calendar date for it.

effluent_limits_001.period: effective date through expiration — one table, no phase-in
effluent_limits_001.design_flow_basis: "Effluent loadings based on average design flow of 130 MGD." (the permit's own note, sheet 4)
effluent_limits_001.arithmetic_check: Every populated loading (kg/day) figure below was recomputed from its paired concentration limit and 130 MGD (= 4.921e8 L/day). Most matched the printed value to within normal rounding — e.g. TSS weekly 40 mg/l -> 19684 kg/day computed vs. 19700 printed; ammonia (Dec-Feb) monthly 6.8 mg/l -> 3346 computed vs. 3350 printed; mercury maximum 1700 ng/l -> 0.837 kg/day computed vs. 0.84 printed (paired to the table's "Daily" loading column, not "Weekly" — see mercury note below); mercury monthly average 3.9 ng/l -> 0.00192 kg/day computed vs. 0.0019 printed. One pair does NOT close this way: shoulder-season (Mar-May & Oct-Nov) ammonia's printed loads of 1780/1190 kg/day recompute from the printed 3.6/2.4 mg/l concentrations to 1772/1181 — a gap too large for rounding, meaning the permit's own loads were computed from unrounded concentration values that were then rounded to 3.6/2.4 for the printed table, not from those printed figures themselves. This is corroboration of the transcription against the document's own arithmetic, not a second source.

bypass_monitoring_603.bypass_trigger_quote: "A CSO-related bypass of the secondary treatment portion (conventional treatment train) of the POTW treatment plant is approved when the flow rate to the POTW treatment plant, as a result of a precipitation event, exceeds 195 MGD and the 25.0 MG Equalization Basin is full. In the event of a CSO-related bypass approved under this condition, the permittee shall minimize the discharge of pollutants to the environment. At a minimum, CSO-related bypass flows must receive primary clarification, solids and floatables removal, and disinfection (when necessary)." (note a, sheet 15)
bypass_monitoring_603.significance: This is the enforceable form of the 195 MGD figure the bound Fact Sheet explains in narrative (Page 6-7 of 40): plant peak hydraulic capacity is 195 MGD through the conventional (secondary) train and 205 MGD through the HRT/Densadeg system, 400 MGD combined. Flow above 195 MGD (and up to 400 MGD) is diverted here rather than through secondary treatment; only above 400 MGD does the headworks bypass (002) engage.

municipal_pretreatment_schedule.due_basis: [inference] — the permit says "no later than 18 months from the effective date of this permit"; 2024-02-01 + 18 months.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.submit_to: Ohio EPA, Central Office Pretreatment Unit and to Ohio EPA, Northwest District Office
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.requirement: Evaluate the adequacy of local industrial user limitations to prevent introduction of pollutants into the POTW that would interfere with its operation, pass through in amounts exceeding water quality standard-based limits, be incompatible with the POTW, or limit wastewater/sludge use options. Submit technical justification for REVISING local limits (with a pretreatment program modification request) or for RETAINING existing ones.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.phosphorus_target: A specific sub-requirement: determine whether local limits for total phosphorus will facilitate "substantial progress toward achieving a monthly average effluent concentration target of 0.5 mg/L." If local limits are deemed inappropriate, the permittee must submit supporting data/evidence for that determination instead. The bound Fact Sheet (Page 16 of 40) frames this as NOT itself an effluent limit.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.pollutants_requiring_justification: Arsenic, cadmium, total chromium, dissolved hexavalent chromium, copper, free cyanide, lead, mercury, molybdenum, nickel, selenium, silver and zinc — "unless screening of wastewater and sludge indicate these pollutants are not present in significant amounts" — plus any other pollutant where a local limit may be necessary to protect against pass through, interference or sludge disposal.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.report_contents: Nine numbered items (i-ix, sheet 19-20): pollutants of concern and justification; plant/industrial flows (incl. hauled-waste data if accepted); domestic/background concentrations (3 locations x 5 days, or 2 locations x 7 days, of domestic-only wastewater); treatment plant removal efficiencies; a comparison of maximum allowable headworks loadings against all applicable criteria; allocation method if limits are revised; narrative/BMP local-limit implementation info if proposed; supporting data/assumptions/methodologies; and, if new/revised limits are proposed, a licensed Ohio PE's stamp and signature.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.revisions: A revised report is due within 90 days of Ohio EPA notifying the permittee of deficiencies; revised limits must be incorporated into all industrial user control documents no later than 4 months after Ohio EPA's approval.
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.sampling_methods: Mercury (d.i): if EPA Method 245.1/245.2 shows domestic background below detection, use EPA Method 1631 or 245.7 instead. Free cyanide (d.ii): use ASTM D7237, OIA-1677-09, or ASTM D4282-02 (the last requires supporting documentation that it meets the 40 CFR 122.44(i)(1)(iv) "sufficiently sensitive" standard).
municipal_pretreatment_schedule.lettering_defect: Report-contents item viii (sheet 20) reads "...used in establishing the information in item 1.a through 1.g above" — but this schedule's own top-level items are lettered only a through d (a. the evaluation/report requirement itself; b. revisions; c. incorporation deadline; d. sampling methods, i-ii above); nothing in this Item goes as far as "1.g." Transcribed as printed; the document's own defect, not corrected here.

status_as_of_2026_08_26.lapsed: The single milestone date (2025-08-01) is in the past as of 2026-08-26.
status_as_of_2026_08_26.what_is_not_established: WHETHER IT WAS FILED. Nothing in this corpus establishes that — no submittal, no acknowledgment, no violation notice, and no ECHO/ICIS extract for this facility is committed. "Past due" here means the date has passed, NOT that the City missed it.
status_as_of_2026_08_26.how_to_close_it: A public-records request to Ohio EPA (Central Office Pretreatment Unit and/or Northwest District Office) for the 52599 submittal under permit 2PF00000 would settle it, and would also show the City's determination on total-phosphorus local limits ahead of the Maumee Watershed TMDL's individual WLA taking hold (see other_requirements_of_note.tmdl_wasteload_allocation below).

other_requirements_of_note.bypass_trigger: See bypass_monitoring_603.bypass_trigger_quote above (Item F is the sheet-15 note; it is not separately re-lettered in Part II).

biomonitoring_program.text: "The permittee shall continue to implement an effluent biomonitoring program to determine the toxicity of the effluent from Station 2PF00000001."
biomonitoring_program.testing: Annual chronic toxicity tests on Ceriodaphnia dubia and Pimephales promelas at outfall 001, with acute endpoints derived from the same chronic tests (not separately dosed). Ambient/control water drawn from upstream station 801. SOP or verification of SOP submittal due no later than three months after the effective date — on or about 2024-05-01 [inference].
biomonitoring_program.definitions: TUa = 100/LC50; TUc = 100/IC25 (or 100/sqrt(NOEC x LOEC) for Ceriodaphnia dubia where more restrictive).

mercury_general_variance.item: X. General Mercury Variance (sheets 31-33), under OAC 3745-33-07(D)(10)
mercury_general_variance.basis: "The City of Toledo has demonstrated that the facility is currently unable to comply with the monthly average water quality based effluent limit of 1.3 ng/l without construction of expensive end-of-pipe controls... The City of Toledo is currently able to achieve an annual average mercury concentration of 12 ng/l."
mercury_general_variance.conditions: Comply with the Part I,A mercury limits (1700 ng/l max, 3.9 ng/l monthly avg — see warnings[2]); make reasonable progress toward the 1.3 ng/l WQBEL via a Pollutant Minimization Program (PMP: household/school mercury collection, thermometer exchange, outreach, low-level sampling, GIS mapping, pretreatment BMPs); use EPA Method 1631 for compliance monitoring; hold annual average <= 12 ng/l; submit an annual PMP report by March 1 (to the NPDES Permit Unit, P.O. Box 1049, Columbus, copied to Ohio EPA Northwest District Office).
mercury_general_variance.exceedance_backstop: If the 12 ng/l annual average is exceeded: notify NW District within 30 days; then EITHER submit an individual-variance application within 6 months OR request a permit modification within 6 months for a compliance schedule. If NEITHER is done, the underlying 1.3 ng/l monthly WQBEL applies at outfall 001 starting 6 months after the exceedance date. This condition does not apply if intake water is shown to be the primary source of the exceedance.
mercury_general_variance.reopener_and_renewal: Ohio EPA may reopen/modify the permit at any time on WQS revisions to the variance (Item Y). Renewal requires the Item X.1.h certification, a PMP progress status report, a list of continuing PMP strategies, and a statement requesting renewal (Item Z) — see stale_cross_references below: Item Z.1 itself misprints this as "Item V.1.h."
mercury_general_variance.stale_cross_references: Two of this Item's own internal cross-references are stale, printed as if pointing to Part II Item V (sheet 29, a sludge percent-solids testing requirement with no ".1.d" or ".1.h" subsection) when they plainly mean Item X itself. (1) Item X.1.h (sheet 32) reads "...as required in Part II, Item V.1.d. of this permit" — the plan-of-study/PMP-continuation clause it means is Item X.1.d (sheet 31, "The permittee shall continue implementing a PMP for mercury consistent with the plan of study..."), i.e. a self-reference that should read X.1.d. (2) Item Z.1 (sheet 33) reads "the certification described under Part II, Item V.1.h." — the certification it means is the one Item X.1.h itself defines (sheet 32), so this too should read X.1.h. Transcribed as printed; the document's own defect, not corrected here.

pretreatment_program.requirement_index: Legal authority; funding/staffing; industrial-user inventory and Significant Industrial User notification (within 30 days of determination, per OAC 3745-3-01(FF)); slug-load control plan evaluation (existing SIUs within 1 year of effective date if never evaluated; new SIUs within 1 year of designation); local limits (see waste_load_allocation_values below); control mechanisms; annual inspection/sampling of all SIUs; annual POTW priority-pollutant monitoring of influent/effluent/sludge; enforcement (annual SNC publication by April 15); reporting (quarterly IU violation report by the 15th of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct; annual pretreatment report by May 15); 3-year record retention (5 for sludge, extended during unresolved litigation); and a 45-day-effective / substantial-modification review process for program changes.
pretreatment_program.waste_load_allocation_values_ug_l_unless: Arsenic 242, Cadmium 11, Chromium (hexavalent) 24, Chromium (total) 250, Copper 38, Cyanide (free) 13, Lead 38, Molybdenum 25 mg/L, Nickel 230, Selenium 12, Silver 3.2, Zinc 328 (sheet 34). Plus a target (not a limit) of 0.5 mg/L total phosphorus.

outfall_signage.requirement: Permanent stream-bank marker at every regulated outfall, bypass and CSO — install within 4 months of effective date if none exists (i.e., on or about 2024-06-01 [inference]). Minimum 2ft x 2ft, 3ft above ground, 2-inch lettering, unobstructed from boats/swimmers/anglers/shore. Combined-sewer outfalls must additionally warn that untreated human sewage may discharge in wet weather with possible harmful bacteria.

storm_water_no_exposure_certification.status_as_of_2026_08_26: NOT YET LAPSED — about 2 months out from today. Distinct from the pretreatment schedule above, which HAS lapsed; recorded so the two due dates aren't conflated.

tmdl_wasteload_allocation.compliance_mechanism: Regulated through the Maumee Watershed Total Phosphorus NPDES General Permit, under which Toledo Bay View WRF has been granted coverage — NOT as a direct numeric limit in this individual permit. "In the event the permittee is no longer covered by the general permit, this individual permit may be modified, or revoked and reissued, to incorporate effluent limits consistent with the wasteload allocation."

quantification_level_note.significance: The permit's own 0.028 mg/l chlorine limit (effluent_limits_001) is BELOW this quantification level; compliance for reported values below the QL follows the Item N averaging rules (zero-substitution for values below OEPA QL when computing an average-limit compliance determination), not a face-value comparison.

cso_regime.citation: Permit 2PF00000*OD, Part II Items E, F, G, H, sheets 21-27; station tables at Part I,B.2 and Item F above

nine_minimum_controls.controls: (1) proper O&M of the collection system and CSO points; (2) maximize collection- system storage of wet-weather flow before allowing a CSO; (3) review/modify the pretreatment program to minimize non-domestic-discharge impact from CSOs; (4) maximize POTW wet-weather treatment capability and flow to the plant; (5) prohibit dry-weather overflows; (6) control solids/floatables in CSO discharge; (7) conduct required CSO inspection/monitoring/reporting; (8) implement pollution-prevention programs targeting CSO contaminant levels; (9) implement public notification for CSO-affected areas, especially beaches/recreation areas.

public_notification.item: G. (sheets 24-26), for CSO discharges to the Lake Erie Basin, per 40 CFR 122.38
public_notification.signage: per Item BB above, at every CSO outfall and impacted public access area
public_notification.health_dept_and_public_notice: Initial notice within 4 hours of becoming aware of a CSO discharge (water body name, location, impacted public access areas, start/end time) to both the local Dept. of Health/other public entities AND the public itself, per the Public Notification Plan; supplemental notice (volume, end time) within 7 days if not already provided.
public_notification.annual_report: Made available to the public on or before May 1 each year (per 40 CFR 122.38(b)); access instructions reported to Ohio EPA Northwest District Office and, by email to NPDES_CSO@epa.gov, to U.S. EPA. Contents: location/receiving water/treatment per CSO point; date/location/duration/volume/cause of each wet- and dry-weather CSO discharge that year; a monitoring-data summary; impacted public-access-area description; representative precipitation (nearest 0.1 in.) tied to each rain- caused discharge; contact info; and a Nine Minimum Controls / long-term control plan implementation summary, including the anticipated average annual CSO count once the LTCP is fully implemented.

sso_reporting.definition: "An overflow, spill, release, or diversion of wastewater from a sanitary sewer system." Explicitly excludes wet-weather CSO discharges. All SSOs are prohibited.
sso_reporting.imminent_danger_sso: Phone Ohio EPA (1-800-282-9378) and the city/county Board of Health within 24 hours of learning of an SSO that may imminently/substantially endanger human health (dry-weather overflows, major line breaks, fish kills, public contact with raw sewage, sensitive-water/high-exposure-area events). Follow-up written report within 5 days: start/stop time, location/ID, receiving water, volume estimate, component that failed, cause, and remediation/mitigation milestones.
sso_reporting.all_ssos: Reported systemwide on the DMR at station 300 (see sso_monitoring_300 above); each location overflowing on a given day = one occurrence. Annual report (all SSOs, including those never reaching state waters) due by March 31: a table of SSO locations (numbered consecutively from 301, noting eliminations), a table of date/ID/receiving-water/volume(MG) per event, and a water-in-basement (WIB) summary by count and sewershed with a narrative pattern analysis (publicly-owned collection system WIBs only).

wet_reasonable_potential.citation: Fact Sheet, Page 15 of 40 (PDF page 65) narrative; Attachment 1, Page 39 of 40 (PDF page 89) table
wet_reasonable_potential.finding: "Reasonable potential" NOT demonstrated for either species, acute or chronic (all four cells of Attachment 1 read "No"). Ceriodaphnia dubia chronic PEQ calculated at 1.6 TUc against a 2.5 TUc WLA; no PEQ could even be calculated for Pimephales promelas or acute Ceriodaphnia dubia because no toxicity was ever detected in those columns. This is WHY the Part I,A table carries toxicity as monitor-only with no numeric limit, and why Part I,C has no TRE schedule.

mercury_variance_calculation.note: The 3.9 ng/l monthly-average variance limit in effluent_limits_001 was calculated as the dataset's PEQmax, chosen over PEQavg as the statistical "best fit." The Fact Sheet attaches three DIFFERENT date ranges in this discussion and they should not be conflated: the PEQavg comparison itself — reporting a drop from 6.6 ng/L (at original-variance issuance) to 2.6 ng/L — is explicitly dated "June 2016 to June 2023" (Page 15 of 40); a separate, earlier finding that the facility "will not meet the 30-day average permit limit of 1.3 ng/l" is based on "monitoring results from June 2016 through June 2021" (Page 14 of 40); and the PEQmax calculation that actually produced the 3.9 ng/l limit is not given its own restated date range in either passage — it is evaluated on "the dataset" discussed immediately after the 2016-2023 PEQavg sentence, but the Fact Sheet does not itself label a period for the PEQmax figure. Cited here as the fact sheet's own language, not verified against any underlying DMR data in this corpus.

table_17_final_effluent_limits.citation: Fact Sheet, Table 17 "Final Effluent Limits for Outfall 001," Page 37 of 40 (PDF page 87); Basis-column legend and footnotes at Page 38 of 40 (PDF page 88)
table_17_final_effluent_limits.role: The Fact Sheet's own restatement of the same outfall-001 limits already transcribed above as effluent_limits_001 — added here as CORROBORATION (same bound PDF, not a second source) because Table 17 independently confirms two things the issued permit's own table doesn't state as plainly: the 130 MGD design-flow basis for every load figure, and which specific rule underlies each of the two mercury numbers.
table_17_final_effluent_limits.corroborates_design_flow: Footnote a: "Effluent loadings based on average design discharge flow of 130 MGD." (worded "average design discharge flow" here vs. the issued permit's own "average design flow" at sheet 4 — same figure, phrased slightly differently in each document.) Confirms design_flow_basis and arithmetic_check above.
table_17_final_effluent_limits.corroborates_mercury_pairing: The Mercury row reads: Concentration 3.9 ng/L (30 Day Average) / 1700 ng/L (Daily Maximum); Loading 0.0019 kg/day (30 Day Average) / 0.84 kg/day (Daily Maximum); Basis "VAR (avg.) / WQS (max)". Per the Basis-column legend, VAR = "Mercury variance (OAC 3745-1-38(J))" and WQS = "Ohio Water Quality Standards (OAC 3745-1)". This is the one place in the whole corpus (permit or Fact Sheet) that states, on a single line, which rule sets which of the two mercury numbers — confirming 3.9 ng/l is the variance-based average limit and 1700 ng/l is the WQS-based maximum limit (see warnings[2] and mercury_variance_calculation above).
table_17_final_effluent_limits.column_label_note: Table 17 heads its columns "30 Day Average" / "Daily Maximum" rather than the issued permit's "Monthly" / "Weekly," but the printed VALUES are identical (e.g. TSS 25/40 mg/L, 12300/19700 kg/day) and footnote d ("7 day average limit") on every "Daily Maximum" figure paired with a "30 Day Average" figure confirms it is in fact the same weekly limit, not a distinct daily one. Not a new set of numbers — a different pair of column headers over the values already transcribed in effluent_limits_001 above.
table_17_final_effluent_limits.basis_by_parameter: Keyed to the effluent_limits_001.limits field names above. water_temperature: M (monitoring-frequency guidance) · dissolved_oxygen: PD (Plant Design) · total_suspended_solids: PD · oil_and_grease: WQS · ammonia_nh3 (all three seasonal limits): WLA/ABS (Wasteload Allocation / Antibacksliding) · nitrogen_kjeldahl_total and nitrite_plus_nitrate_total: BTJ (Best Technical Judgment) · phosphorus_total: PTS (Phosphorus Treatment Standards) · orthophosphate_dissolved: PMR (Phosphorus Monitoring Requirements) · nickel/zinc/cadmium/lead/chromium/copper_total_recoverable and chromium_dissolved_hexavalent: M · trichlorophenol_246: RP (Reasonable Potential) · e_coli, ph_maximum, ph_minimum: WQS · flow_rate: M · chlorine_total_residual (both seasons): WLA/PD · mercury_total_low_level: "VAR (avg.) / WQS (max)" — see corroborates_mercury_pairing above · cyanide_free_low_level and residue_total_filterable: M · acute/chronic toxicity (both species, all four limit rows): WET · cbod_5_day: PD.
